decisions.name: Balnarring Market
decisions.context: Balnarring Bakehouse is the village bakery the Balnarring side of the Peninsula has relied on for years. The pies and pastries are proper country-bakery standard, a solid beef-and-mushroom, an honest custard tart, a vanilla slice that will not disappoint anyone over the age of eight, and the weekend breakfast sandwich has become the quiet fuel source for half the Balnarring Market crowd on a Saturday morning.

decisions.name: Red Hill Cheese
decisions.context: A good fifteen-minute detour on a hinterland loop. Pair it with Red Hill Cheese around the corner or a cellar door on the ridge for a proper Peninsula food afternoon.

decisions.name: Safety Beach
decisions.context: Martha’s Table Restaurant overlooks the marina at Safety Beach. The operator describes Mediterranean cooking shaped by seasonal produce, with lunch and dinner services on selected days.

decisions.name: Elgee Park
decisions.context: Merricks Store is a village bistro, wine store and produce stop. The operator serves breakfast and lunch daily, with tables by the fire or on the decks. Its wine list centres on Elgee Park and Baillieu vineyards, alongside other local producers.

decisions.name: Hotel Sorrento
decisions.context: Hotel Sorrento has been part of the town since 1872. The hotel is at 5–15 Hotham Road, above Port Phillip Bay. Its current operator offers restaurants and bars alongside accommodation, with separate dining spaces for different kinds of visit. Check the current dining options and book the space that suits your group.

decisions.name: Safety Beach
decisions.context: Balnarring Beach and Mount Martha Beach. Both have shallow, calm bay water, easy parking, and low-pressure atmospheres. Safety Beach is a solid third option.

decisions.name: Bushrangers Bay
decisions.context: From the eastern carpark at Cape Schanck Lighthouse, this walk leads through coastal scrub to Bushrangers Bay. Parks Victoria describes a 5.4 km return trip taking about two hours. Allow more time for stops and the return climb: the sandy, narrow, unsealed path includes steep stairs.

decisions.name: Bushrangers Bay
decisions.context: Walk it in sections. Cape Schanck north toward Tootgarook (about 13 km one-way, half a day, transport coordination needed at the far end) is the section we rate. Cape Schanck to Bushrangers Bay and back is the reliable half-day; Diamond Bay to London Bridge is the quieter one. Orange markers show the through-track direction. Check tides before setting off: some lower sections flood at high tide and need the inland bypass.

decisions.name: Safety Beach
decisions.context: Midday: Drive to Mount Martha Beach or Safety Beach for a bay swim. Lunch from Dromana food options.

decisions.name: Point Nepean
decisions.context: Afternoon: Portsea Front Beach and Portsea Hotel, or Point Nepean fort walk.

decisions.name: Bushrangers Bay
decisions.context: Morning: Cape Schanck boardwalk and Bushrangers Bay walk (combined, 2–3 hours).

decisions.name: Peninsula Hot Springs
decisions.context: Late morning/midday: Drive 15 minutes to Peninsula Hot Springs for an afternoon session (book in advance).

decisions.name: Safety Beach
decisions.context: Balnarring Beach and Safety Beach are the best bay beaches for children under 8.

decisions.name: Cape Schanck
decisions.context: Cape Schanck boardwalk - Short, flat, dramatic. Children understand what they're looking at immediately - the blowholes and sea platforms are engaging without narration. 30–40 minutes round trip.

decisions.name: Safety Beach
decisions.context: Bayside spine: Nepean Highway → Point Nepean Road - the busier road, threading through Mornington, Safety Beach, Dromana, Rosebud, Rye, Sorrento, and Portsea. Most cafes, shops, and beach carparks are off this road.

decisions.name: Safety Beach
decisions.context: Nepean Highway (A3) follows the eastern shore of Port Phillip Bay from Frankston south through Mornington, Mount Martha, Safety Beach, Dromana, and Rosebud. Genuinely beautiful on a clear morning. On a Friday afternoon in peak season, it's stationary through Mornington and Dromana.

decisions.name: Safety Beach
decisions.context: Key towns: Mornington, Mount Martha, Safety Beach, Dromana, Rosebud

decisions.name: Bushrangers Bay
decisions.context: Cape Schanck is where the Peninsula finally runs out of land, dropping off the plateau into Bass Strait with a drama that still takes first-timers by surprise. The 1859 lighthouse stands on the last headland, the boardwalk threads down through tea-tree to a basalt beach that disappears at high tide, and on a clear afternoon the horizon carries nothing but open ocean all the way to Tasmania. This is the Peninsula's most cinematic short walk, and the cleanest case for why the southern end is worth the drive beyond the vineyards. Come for the lighthouse and the lookout, stay for the Bushrangers Bay walk west along the coast, and time your arrival for the last two hours of daylight.

decisions.name: Elgee Park
decisions.context: Merricks North is a rural wine-country locality with Jackalope, Rare Hare and Scorpo among its visitor destinations. Elgee Park is here too, but its estate is closed to the general public.

decisions.name: Safety Beach
decisions.context: Safety Beach is a bayside township on the Mornington Peninsula's eastern Port Phillip shoreline, 70 km from Melbourne, between Dromana and Mount Martha, with a marina and a sheltered swimming beach.

decisions.name: St Andrews Beach Brewery
decisions.context: St Andrews Beach is a quiet back-beach settlement between Rye Ocean Beach and Gunnamatta Surf Beach. Its draw is the exposed Bass Strait coast: dunes, rock pools and long walks when conditions allow. Parks Victoria describes a short sandy path from the car park with a steep descent to the shore. The beach is unpatrolled, with dangerous rips, currents and reefs; swimming is not recommended. Keep to marked paths around the dunes and check park conditions before visiting. The St Andrews Beach Brewery and golf course share the place name but list their addresses in nearby Fingal, so allow a separate drive for either.

decisions.name: Peninsula Hot Springs
decisions.context: Peninsula Hot Springs and Alba Thermal Springs operate in all weather; wet conditions are, for many visitors, their best.

decisions.name: Safety Beach
decisions.context: Safety Beach is the Peninsula's most reliably calm swimming beach - the name is genuinely accurate - and the right answer when you have a young family, a nervous swimmer, or simply want to walk along a long flat shoreline without the theatre of the back beaches. The water is shallow, warm even by April standards, and the bay rarely produces any real chop along this stretch.

decisions.name: Hotel Sorrento
decisions.context: One of the Peninsula's genuinely memorable experiences. Combine it with a late lunch at The Baths or Hotel Sorrento on the way back.

decisions.name: Bushrangers Bay
decisions.context: 8. Bushrangers Bay walk

decisions.name: Point Nepean
decisions.context: Point Nepean National Park covers the peninsula's western tip - a former quarantine station and military base, now open as a national park. The Point Nepean fort walk is the main circuit. Park entry is free; the optional shuttle is ticketed.

decisions.name: Safety Beach
decisions.context: Both Balnarring Beach and Mount Martha Beach offer bay-side calm water swimming in a lower-crowd setting than Sorrento or Safety Beach. Balnarring suits families with toddlers; Mount Martha has better cafés nearby. Full guide at the Peninsula's best beaches.

decisions.name: Bushrangers Bay
decisions.context: Cape Schanck boardwalk for the best effort-to-payoff ratio. Bushrangers Bay for the best uncrowded experience. Two Bays Walking Track for the best full-day walk.

decisions.name: Hotel Sorrento
decisions.context: Accommodation is the largest line: mid-range self-contained places sit in the middle of the market, and premium properties (Jackalope, Hotel Sorrento) run to roughly double that on a summer weekend. Add hot springs entry, meals, and activities on top. Summer and long weekends carry a premium; autumn midweek is the cheapest way to do the same trip. See the default Peninsula weekend for the full worked plan.

decisions.name: Georgie Bass
decisions.context: Three: lunch at Georgie Bass. The cafe is open until 2:30pm on weekdays and 3pm on weekends, which means you have time to do the walk properly before arriving for food. The all-day menu runs on regional produce from the owners’ own farm: seasonal egg dishes, proper sourdough, vegetable preparations that understand what they are. The outdoor courtyard works in most weather. Coffee is Commonfolk. It is a cafe rather than a restaurant, and the difference matters less than you would expect when the produce is this considered.

decisions.name: Flinders Hotel
decisions.context: Flinders Hotel is the default, and it is a better default than its reputation suggests. The rooms are clean, contemporary, and well-sized. The location puts you inside the village rather than on the edge of it. The attached pub gives the whole place a useful looseness: you can come back from a walk, sit at the bar for an hour, and not feel like you are performing a hotel stay.

decisions.name: Bushrangers Bay
decisions.context: The landscape is more interesting in cold weather, too. The bay goes slate grey. The ridge mist hangs until lunchtime. The sea at Bushrangers Bay gets bigger and the cliffs behind it get blacker. The Peninsula in a southerly is one of the most underrated coastal landscapes in southern Australia.

decisions.name: Flinders Hotel
decisions.context: Pick a base with a fireplace. More important in winter than in any other season. The stays where the weekend actually lands are the ones where the room is warm before you come back to it. Lindenderry has rooms with working hearths. Crittenden Villas have them. Polperro Villas have them. Peninsula Hot Springs Glamping is a more dramatic version of the same principle: tented suites with wood stoves and private hot tubs are at their best in July, not January. On a lower budget, the rooms at Flinders Hotel or Hotel Sorrento with bay views work well, because the view itself is doing some of the mood work in winter weather.

decisions.name: Hotel Sorrento
decisions.context: Pick a base with a fireplace. More important in winter than in any other season. The stays where the weekend actually lands are the ones where the room is warm before you come back to it. Lindenderry has rooms with working hearths. Crittenden Villas have them. Polperro Villas have them. Peninsula Hot Springs Glamping is a more dramatic version of the same principle: tented suites with wood stoves and private hot tubs are at their best in July, not January. On a lower budget, the rooms at Flinders Hotel or Hotel Sorrento with bay views work well, because the view itself is doing some of the mood work in winter weather.

decisions.name: Red Hill Brewery
decisions.context: After the walk and travel: Lunch at a cellar door with a fire. Reserve a time that allows for the full return walk, stops and the drive to lunch. The move that shapes the whole day. Ten Minutes by Tractor for the high-end version. Montalto if you want the sculpture grounds around you, even wet. Polperro for an underrated mid-winter dining room in Red Hill. Red Hill Brewery for the low-key version with a wood pizza oven and a hop garden behind you.

decisions.name: Red Hill Cheese
decisions.context: 9am: Cheese shop, chocolate shop, bakery. Winter Sunday mornings on the Peninsula are for the producers. Red Hill Cheese, Mornington Peninsula Chocolates, and a bakery stop are the right sequence. You are taking winter home in a cooler bag.

decisions.name: Safety Beach
decisions.context: Dromana sits on Port Phillip Bay between Safety Beach and McCrae, at the foot of Arthurs Seat. This is where the land lifts. The beach stretches long and practical on one side, Arthurs Seat rises immediately behind, and the roads up into the hinterland begin almost as soon as the shops thin out. That geography makes Dromana one of the Peninsula’s better base towns, especially for visitors who want range without paying for a more romantic postcode.

decisions.name: Foxeys Hangout
decisions.context: The food-and-drink strength here is proximity to estates behind town. Crittenden is one of the region’s benchmark producers and an easy inclusion in a Dromana-based day. Foxeys Hangout and other nearby ridge addresses can also be folded in.

decisions.name: Flinders Sourdough
decisions.context: Flinders Sourdough is the right opening move. It is how you tune yourself to the place. Get there before the middle of the morning, buy what looks best, and eat it outside if the weather allows.

decisions.name: Flinders Hotel
decisions.context: Flinders Hotel is more useful than glamorous, and that is meant as praise. A pub meal or drink here makes sense after a windy morning walk, and it feels grounded rather than aspirational.

decisions.name: Flinders General Store
decisions.context: The Flinders General Store is ideal for provisions, coffee and low-fuss staples.

decisions.name: Ten Minutes by Tractor
decisions.context: Ten Minutes by Tractor is the Main Ridge lunch to build around if food matters most. The wine, the point of view, and the confidence all justify the drive. Give it room rather than bolting three more bookings around it.

decisions.name: Red Hill Estate
decisions.context: Red Hill Estate is a Main Ridge cellar door with a long view across the Peninsula. It feels properly of the place: less polished than some neighbours, more convincing for it. For a tasting that still feels like wine country rather than a production, start here.

decisions.name: Paringa Estate
decisions.context: Paringa Estate is in Red Hill South, while Quealy is in Balnarring. Both require a separate drive if you want to extend the day beyond Main Ridge.

decisions.name: Merricks General Wine Store
decisions.context: Merricks General Wine Store is the address that tells you what Merricks is about. Local without being scruffy, smart without self-conscious, exactly the kind of room you wish more regions had. If you only have one booking here, make it this.

decisions.name: Small Stone Pantry
decisions.context: Jetty Road’s spring seasonal taps are the reason to visit right now rather than on any other weekend. The head brewer uses the rotating list to take risks - expect a dry-hopped lager or a single-hop pale built around a new-season Australian hop variety, the kind of thing that won’t appear in cans. The taproom is the most considered fit-out of the bayside breweries: polished concrete, a generous deck that catches the afternoon north-westerly, and a kitchen running wood-fired flatbreads that hold up against the hoppier pours. Ask the bar staff what came on this week specifically. The seasonals move fast and a Friday afternoon tap can be gone by Sunday. Allow two hours minimum if you want food. No booking required for walk-ins, though the deck fills by 1pm on a warm Saturday. Pair the afternoon with a stop at Small Stone Pantry in Dromana for provisions on the way home.

decisions.name: Johnny Ripe
decisions.context: Foxeys pours its biodynamic sparkling flight outdoors when the weather allows, and right now the weather allows. The deck faces north across the Red Hill slope, and the vines are just breaking bud - the right moment to sit in front of the sparkling flight and understand why Chris Strickland’s program produces wines that taste unlike anything else on the Peninsula. The flight runs through the range before you commit to a bottle, which is the correct order of operations. The Blanc de Blancs is the one to linger on: taut, mineral, and genuinely dry in a way that most regional fizz is not. The biodynamic certification is visible in the vineyard right now, cover crops and all. Spring is when that farming choice reads most clearly in the glass. Allow ninety minutes. Book ahead for weekend sessions - walk-ins have been turned away on busy Saturdays. Pair the visit with lunch at Johnny Ripe nearby.

decisions.name: Tessellation Folding Workshop with Jacky Cheng
decisions.context: Orizome is the Japanese practice of folding and dyeing washi paper, and the Mornington Peninsula Regional Gallery is running a free two-hour session on Saturday afternoon. The process involves folding paper tightly, dipping the folded edges into dye, and opening the sheet to reveal a pattern you cannot fully predict. It is hands-on and accessible regardless of prior experience; no background in paper arts is needed. The gallery’s program is quietly one of the best practical arts offerings on the Peninsula, and free workshops with this level of craft specificity are not common. The Saturday morning Tessellation Folding Workshop with Jacky Cheng runs 9:30 am–12:30 pm at the same venue if you want to make a full day of it.

decisions.name: Bushrangers Bay
decisions.context: The boardwalk from Cape Schanck lighthouse to Bushrangers Bay is a 30-to-40-minute walk each way, and late October is the correct time to do it. The coastal heath on either side - banksias, tea-tree, native pigface running across the dune faces - is in active flower right now. By February it will be scorched and grey. The track descends from the lighthouse carpark, crosses the headland, and drops toward the rocky bay platform at the end. It is exposed and the surface is uneven in sections; wear proper footwear. Go in the morning before the southerly fills in. The lighthouse itself is run by Parks Victoria and is worth a quick look before you descend. Cape Schanck Road, Cape Schanck. Entry to the park requires a parks pass; check the Parks Victoria website. Allow two hours return.

decisions.name: Bushrangers Bay
decisions.context: The coastal heathland between Cape Schanck Lighthouse and Bushrangers Bay is at its peak density of wildflower cover through November. Ground orchids, sun orchids, and tea-tree in full white flower line both sides of the boardwalk before it drops toward the basalt platforms. The light at this end of the Peninsula is different from the bay side - harder, cleaner, and in spring the offshore wind is light enough that the platforms are walkable at low tide without getting pushed around. The circuit from the lighthouse carpark out to the Bushrangers Bay lookout and back takes about 90 minutes at an easy pace. Go before 10am to get the low-angle light on the rock platforms and to avoid the mid-morning coach groups that arrive at the lighthouse from late October onward.

decisions.context: First, the honest note. Winter on the Peninsula, or any genuinely wet weekend, will shut down a few of the options you might have been counting on. Most of the smaller beach kiosks will be closed. Some of the boutique cellar doors drop to reduced hours. The winery restaurants with outdoor terraces become less interesting because the terraces are not the point anymore. And a handful of the coastal walks get genuinely dangerous when the wind picks up, Bushrangers Bay and the Cape Schanck boardwalk are both worth checking the conditions on before you commit.

decisions.context: Red Hill Brewery. Considering Red Hill Brewery for lunch? Check the brewery’s current food service, menu and opening days before planning your stop. Confirm covered seating directly if you need a wet-weather option.

decisions.name: Hotel Sorrento
decisions.context: Food: Food trucks line Ocean Beach Road. The quality is good - this is not a carnival situation. Local producers are also selling: cheese, bread, wine, cider. The Hotel Sorrento and the Continental both have kitchens running but will be at capacity. Book if you want a table. Otherwise, eat from the trucks and do not complain.

decisions.name: Peninsula Hot Springs
decisions.context: A morning tee time gets you off the course by mid-afternoon. That leaves the second half of the day for a late lunch on the Red Hill plateau (Montalto piazza is the easiest walk-up), a hot springs session (Peninsula Hot Springs or Alba, 15 minutes away), or a coastal walk at Cape Schanck.

decisions.name: Safety Beach
decisions.context: Safety Beach. The name is accurate. Long, shallow, gentle water and a foreshore that runs for kilometres. The first choice with toddlers and nervous swimmers.

decisions.name: Point Nepean
decisions.context: Point Nepean National Park. The fort tunnels, the quarantine station and the views across the heads are a genuine adventure for older children. Ride the main path or use the Parks Victoria shuttle, which adds services in peak periods such as Christmas and the summer school holidays. Leave the car at the entrance and treat it as a half day; our Point Nepean half-day plan sets it out.

decisions.name: Arthurs Seat Eagle
decisions.context: Arthurs Seat. The gondola over the treetops is a reliable hit with younger children. Our Arthurs Seat Eagle guide covers tickets and timing.

decisions.name: Mornington
decisions.context: The big, beautiful estates with lawns and restaurants are excellent places to spend a long lunch. But the experience of understanding what the Peninsula actually grows, the structural pinot noir, the tight chardonnay, the lesser-known Italian varieties, tends to happen in smaller rooms, at smaller tables, with the people who actually made the wine doing the pouring. For the broader landscape of what’s poured on the Peninsula, the Mornington Peninsula winery guide and The Producer Trail are the wider companion pieces to this short list.

decisions.name: Mornington Racecourse Market
decisions.context: If it is the second Saturday of the month, start at the Mornington Farmers’ Market in Mornington Park, listed by Main Street Mornington from 8am to 1pm. This is separate from the Mornington Racecourse Market, usually held on the second Sunday. Confirm the current date and stallholder list before planning your meal around a particular ingredient.

decisions.name: Red Hill Brewery
decisions.context: If the group includes anyone who drinks spirits or cares about beer, there is one stop worth making on the way back to the rental: either Red Hill Brewery for a four-pack of the Scotch Ale (one of the better dark beers brewed in Victoria) or Bass & Flinders Distillery in Tuerong for a bottle of gin and, if you have not tried it, a small paddle tasting of the cask-aged spirits. The distillery tasting is twenty minutes and does not burn through the palate the way a wine tasting does.

decisions.name: Hotel Sorrento
decisions.context: Hotel Sorrento is the working alternative  -  less design-forward, better value, and arguably the best bay view in the town. The bistro on the ground floor is the right place for the first night’s dinner when you have come straight off the freeway and want something direct.

decisions.name: Bushrangers Bay
decisions.context: The landscape is distinctive. The Peninsula’s hinterland is a patchwork of coastal scrub, vineyard rows, and remnant eucalypt bush, and all three of those layers come back into life dramatically in September. The heath on the way to Bushrangers Bay is flowering through late September. The Greens Bush area on the Two Bays walking track has wildflowers through October. The vineyards are at their most architectural in spring: the bare trellises from winter acquire a pale green fringe that transforms the entire plateau over about ten days.

decisions.name: Flinders Hotel
decisions.context: 4pm: Arrive at your base. Spring rooms are both available and cheaper than the autumn equivalents. Lindenderry is particularly good in spring because the gardens are in their early bloom, and the dining room is transitioning from winter stews to spring produce. Polperro Villas and Crittenden Villas are both well-placed for a ridge-focused weekend. Flinders Hotel is the bayside-to-Cape alternative, and in spring the Cape Schanck weather is typically kinder than in autumn.

decisions.name: Red Hill Cheese
decisions.context: 3pm: Producer loop or lookout. A quick loop on the way back down the ridge: Main Ridge Dairy, Red Hill Cheese, and, if the day is warm enough, a quick stop at Arthurs Seat Eagle for the gondola ride. The spring view from the summit is among the clearest of the year, with the bay, the vineyards, and the horizon between Melbourne and the Bellarine in sharp focus.

decisions.name: Johnny Ripe
decisions.context: 10.30am: A late coffee. Commonfolk in Mornington or Johnny Ripe in Red Hill, depending on where your drive home starts.

decisions.name: Bushrangers Bay
decisions.context: Saturday. One serious booking. Book lunch on the ridge, somewhere the villa delivers you to and not the other way around. Walk before lunch if the weather is fair; the Bushrangers Bay walk is the one that sets up the meal properly. Come back to the villa in the afternoon. Bath. Fire. Cheese board and the rest of yesterday’s bottle. Dinner in your own kitchen. The aim is to be horizontal by 9pm.

decisions.name: Bushrangers Bay
decisions.context: PAPP poison baiting and trapping is active in the Mornington Peninsula National Park, including the Bushrangers Bay walk corridor, until October 2026. Dogs are not permitted here. This is a hard prohibition. Antidote for PAPP poisoning: methylene blue. Contact a vet immediately.

decisions.name: Flinders Hotel
decisions.context: Walk + Flinders lunch: 15 minutes north to Flinders village. Flinders Hotel (pub, dog-friendly beer garden if you do not have a dog with you), Moke Dining (one-hat, Fri–Sun dinner/lunch).

decisions.name: Safety Beach
decisions.context: The Baths at Safety Beach, Tassells Cove end, casual cafe format near the beach. Lower price point, suitable for a quick lunch rather than a full dining sit-down.

decisions.name: Flinders Hotel
decisions.context: Flinders Hotel. The best pub on the Peninsula for a walk-in lunch, and the reasons are not complicated: the dining room is large enough that it rarely fills completely, the kitchen takes pub food seriously without trying to be a restaurant, the beer garden faces the village green, and Flinders itself is a town that rewards a wander before or after. Order the parma or the fish, drink the local pale ale, and sit outside if the weather holds. This is the Peninsula pub that works every time.

decisions.name: Johnny Ripe
decisions.context: Johnny Ripe. A café and produce store in Red Hill that serves fast, seasonal, walk-in food. Good for the midday stop when the bigger kitchens are booked.

decisions.name: Red Hill Brewery
decisions.context: Red Hill Brewery. The original and still the most family-friendly. Wood-fired pizza, a hop garden, indoor and outdoor seating, and beer flights that rival the wine tastings down the road. Walk-in tables are available most of the time, including weekends.

decisions.name: St Andrews Beach Brewery
decisions.context: St Andrews Beach Brewery. Larger, louder, more ambitious in its food than most Peninsula breweries. The space is a converted shed that handles groups well. Walk-in availability is usually fine outside of Saturday evening.

decisions.name: Jetty Road Brewery
decisions.context: Jetty Road Brewery. The Dromana outpost. Good beer, a solid food menu, and a useful walk-in fallback for the northern end of the Peninsula when the winery restaurants are full.

decisions.name: Hotel Sorrento
decisions.context: Hotel Sorrento keeps you near the village and bay. The operator lists bay views for its Classic Rooms and township-to-bay views for Sorrento Studios; confirm the view attached to the room you book. Go downstairs for a drink before dinner and keep the village weekend on foot.

decisions.name: Flinders Hotel
decisions.context: Flinders Hotel is underrated because it does not perform luxury in the contemporary sense. That is precisely why it works. It is a clean, comfortable village base at the ocean end of the Peninsula and a very good starting point for people who want sea air in the morning and lunch inland later.

decisions.name: Bushrangers Bay
decisions.context: PAPP poison baiting is active from Portsea Ocean Beach through Greens Bush until October 2026. Dogs are not permitted in any Mornington Peninsula National Park area, including Cape Schanck walking tracks, Bushrangers Bay, Greens Bush, and Point Nepean. Antidote: methylene blue. Contact a vet immediately if ingestion is suspected.

decisions.name: Safety Beach
decisions.context: Safety Beach foreshore: flat foreshore between Safety Beach and Martha Cove. Connects naturally to Tassells Cove (year-round off-leash) without needing to drive between stops.

decisions.name: Red Hill Brewery
decisions.context: Red Hill / Main Ridge area: several farm tracks and reserve walks run through the hinterland. On-leash. This zone pairs well with a cellar-door visit at the confirmed dog-friendly wineries nearby (Stonier, Main Ridge Estate, Red Hill Brewery).

decisions.name: Flinders Hotel
decisions.context: Village walk + pub or café: Flinders village has a flat foreshore circuit and beach access at the Western Port north end (Flinders Beach: off-leash year-round between Dodds Creek and Manton Creek). Combine with Flinders Hotel beer garden or Georgie Bass outdoor seating.

decisions.name: Georgie Bass
decisions.context: Village walk + pub or café: Flinders village has a flat foreshore circuit and beach access at the Western Port north end (Flinders Beach: off-leash year-round between Dodds Creek and Manton Creek). Combine with Flinders Hotel beer garden or Georgie Bass outdoor seating.

decisions.name: Flinders Hotel
decisions.context: Flinders Hotel is the obvious base because it understands the town's scale. This is not the place to hunt for a huge accommodation set. It is the place to base a quieter ocean-side Peninsula weekend correctly.

decisions.name: Flinders Hotel
decisions.context: Quarters sits behind Flinders Hotel, giving you a village base near the bakery, shops and pier. Book the room through Quarters and make a separate reservation if you want to eat at the pub. Moke Dining is another village dinner choice when its service suits your dates.

decisions.name: Hotel Sorrento
decisions.context: Hotel Sorrento is an adults-only stay and guest pool above Sorrento village. Its five room families are Classic, Poolside, Coastal, Sorrento Studios and Sunset Suites; views, terraces and baths vary by room. As checked 3 October 2026, the hotel warns of possible daytime midweek construction noise and changed movement around the property ahead of its 1 December expansion.

decisions.name: Elgee Park
decisions.context: Elgee Park says its estate is closed to the general public. Community groups can arrange a vineyard and sculpture-park tour with the operator. Its wines are available for tasting and sales at Merricks Store, 3460 Frankston-Flinders Road, Merricks. Do not travel to the estate for an ordinary cellar-door visit; check the operator for any arranged tour.

decisions.name: Flinders Hotel
decisions.context: Most people who visit Flinders for wine come for one cellar door plus the village: the Flinders Hotel for lunch, the bakery for the drive home, the coastal walk to clear the head. That's the model - wine as one move in a slower, ocean-edge weekend rather than a cellar-door crawl.

decisions.name: Garagiste
decisions.context: Garagiste is Barnaby Flanders' small-batch Peninsula wine project. The existing Mount Eliza address should not be treated as a public drop-in cellar door: current tasting access and visitor hours have not been verified with the operator. The producer remains active, but this record is paused as a visit recommendation until its public visitor arrangements are confirmed.

decisions.name: Kerri Greens
decisions.context: Kerri Greens says its former cellar door has closed. The producer continues to sell wine online and appears at local markets and pop-ups, with current appearances listed by the operator. There is no public cellar-door address to visit. This record is paused as a visit recommendation until an operator-confirmed visitor location exists.

decisions.name: Kerri Greens
decisions.context: Pt. Leo Estate is the most ambitious project on the Peninsula: a sculpture park, three restaurants, and a producer in its own right. Stonier is the oldest established estate. Scorpo, Paradigm Hill and Kerri Greens are the newer generation working with conviction.

decisions.name: Tar Barrel Brewery & Distillery
decisions.context: The current visitor venue at 72 Watt Road is Tar Barrel Brewery & Distillery. Its operator describes Matt Bebe and Andrew Gow continuing to brew at this address, now alongside a gin and whisky distillery.

decisions.name: Red Hill Brewery
decisions.context: Red Hill Brewery is the oldest serious craft brewery on the Peninsula and still one of the few in Australia that grows its own hops. That detail matters: the farm-to-glass story here is not marketing, it is infrastructure. Dave and Karen Golding planted the hop garden in 2005 and have been making Belgian-style ales from it ever since, witbier, dubbel, tripel, and the seasonal fresh-hop beers that are worth waiting for.

decisions.name: St Andrews Beach Brewery
decisions.context: St Andrews Beach Brewery occupies a former racehorse training property, the brew house sits roughly where the stables once stood, and the lawns extend out toward what was the exercise track. The setting alone would pull visitors, but the operation earns its reputation through the food and the beer in equal measure.
